column1: # Reds in main's whole gate (gate-logs/<sha12>/<stamp>/full-main) that are explained, so push-main.sh's pause
# rule lets landings through them. One line each: the log ref, a tab, what caused it and what fixed it.

column2: UNEXPLAINED, under investigation (lifted by @system_adamic 19:59 MDT; no landing caused it): internal/native TestWASI/regions.a, the oracle's Node leg running the source failed "CompileError: WebAssembly.Module(): Compiling function #481 failed: not enough arguments on the stack for block (need 5, got 0)" (a 1.4 MB module inside Node; the WASI leg passed). 1 red in 4 runs on the Threadripper: the full run, then regions.a alone and whole TestWASI twice (37/0/0 each, SDK clang, load 196 to 292) pass. V8 validation is deterministic, so the bytes differed on that run: open checks with developer tools are emission determinism (20 emits, half under load) and shared on-disk artifacts written without a cross-process lock. TestWASI now keeps module bytes and hash on failure.
